new_scholarship.name: Scholarships for talented students from all over the world
new_scholarship.official_source: Ministry of Education, Research, Development and Youth of the Slovak Republic
new_scholarship.duration: 3 academic years — ten monthly payments in each of the first three academic years of full-time bachelor's or combined bachelor's and master's study (academic years 2026/2027 to 2028/2029)
new_scholarship.deadline: The application deadline for the 2026/2027 round was extended to "8 September 2026, 23:59 CEST". The published original deadline in the official application-procedure guide was 31 July 2026, 16:00 CEST. Registration is now closed.
new_scholarship.application_period: The 2026/2027 call opened during 2026 and closed on 8 September 2026 at 23:59 CEST, extended from the original deadline of 31 July 2026 at 16:00 CEST. No opening or closing date for a 2027/2028 round was published at the time of verification.
new_scholarship.application_method: Separate competitive application submitted by the student exclusively online through the information system at https://scholarships.portalvs.sk/registration. The award is not automatic on admission, and the ministry states that it is not possible to request the scholarship via email. The applicant must separately apply for admission directly to the chosen higher education institution, because receiving the scholarship does not mean acceptance or enrolment at a higher education institution.
new_scholarship.description: The Ministry of Education, Research, Development and Youth of the Slovak Republic awards national scholarships to talented students from all over the world, including Slovaks living abroad, to study at selected public and state higher education institutions in Slovakia. For the 2026/2027 round the ministry allocated 170 bachelor's-level scholarships: 110 financed from the EU co-financed national project for institutions outside the Bratislava region and 60 financed from the state budget for institutions in the Bratislava region. The award is a living allowance of EUR 500 per month paid for ten months in each of the first three academic years of full-time bachelor's or combined bachelor's and master's study, up to EUR 15,000 in total. Selection is made solely on the applicant's percentile score on either the SAT or the SCIO tests, and the study programme must appear on the published SK RIS3 2021+ list.
new_scholarship.best_fit: Applicants holding citizenship of a country other than Slovakia, or Slovaks living abroad holding the certificate under Section 7 of Act No. 474/2005 Coll., who completed their secondary education outside Slovakia, have sat the SAT or the SCIO tests, and intend to enrol in a full-time SK RIS3 2021+ programme at a Slovak public or state higher education institution. It suits applicants who can fund tuition fees, health insurance, travel and living costs beyond a EUR 500 monthly allowance, and who are willing to study in Slovak or in a foreign-language programme at an institution that may lie outside the Bratislava region. It does not suit applicants who need a scholarship that covers tuition, who want to study a field outside the SK RIS3 list, who have previously studied at a Slovak secondary school or higher education institution, or who cannot sit a standardised test.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Eligibility is decided by nationality, residence, prior study history and a standardised-test threshold, not by financial need or by a broader merit review. The applicant must hold citizenship of a country other than Slovakia, evidenced by a notarised copy of a passport or, for citizens of the European Union, the European Economic Area and Switzerland, a national identity card; dual nationality that includes Slovak is allowed, and Slovaks living abroad may qualify by submitting the certificate issued under Section 7 of Act No. 474/2005 Coll. on Slovaks Living Abroad. The applicant must have had no permanent residence in Slovakia between 1 January 2021 and the application deadline, must not have been a pupil or graduate of a secondary school located in Slovakia, and, at the bachelor's level, must not previously have studied at a higher education institution in Slovakia other than through academic mobility. The applicant must apply to a public or state higher education institution in Slovakia for a supported full-time, in-person study programme on the SK RIS3 2021+ list, and must meet one of two test thresholds: an SAT total score of at least 1100 points, or an average percentile of at least 63 across the two SCIO tests in Mathematics (MAT) and General Academic Prerequisites (VŠP). There is no upper age limit; applicants under 18 need a hand-signed consent from their legal guardian, and the ministry states that exceptions to these conditions cannot be granted.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: Selection is decided exclusively by the standardised-test result, which the ministry states is the only criterion for awarding the scholarship. The SAT and SCIO results are converted to a common percentile scale of 0 to 100 so that applicants who sat different tests are ranked together, and the ministry publishes the conversion table in Annex 12 of the methodological document. Within each funding source, applicants are first ranked by percentile score inside their regional subgroup: 10 per cent of the allocated scholarships of that source, that is 50 per cent of the total across the five subgroups, is awarded to the highest-ranked applicant of each subgroup, and the remaining 50 per cent is then awarded by percentile score alone with no regional redressement. Regional redistribution is applied only where the number of eligible applications exceeds the number of scholarships allocated for the level and funding source, and each funding source is ranked separately. The scholarship is paid only after enrolment, and the ministry or the higher education institution verifies eligibility and the authenticity of documents; falsified or altered documents result in withdrawal from the scholarship and repayment of amounts already awarded.

new_scholarship.notes: SCOPE AND IDENTITY. The official award name is "Scholarships for talented students from all over the world", which is the heading of the call page and the wording used by the ministry; the ministry's own Slovak-language scheme title translates as scholarships for foreign talented students from all corners of the world including Slovaks living abroad. No acronym or short form is in general official use, so short_title-level naming is given in notes rather than invented: the ministry's own national project title is "Provision of scholarships for talented domestic and international students for the purpose of their studies at Higher Education Institutions in Slovakia". The award is a national government scheme, not a university award, and it is not listed in the do-not-duplicate protocol. THE SLOT 03 OVERLAP. A separate record, b01, covers the MAECI scholarships for foreign students of Italian citizenship abroad (research/bachelor/b01-maeci-scholarships-foreign-students-italian-citizens-abroad.json). It is a different award, a different country and a different awarding body; this file leaves that record untouched and holds no reference to it beyond this note. DEGREE LEVEL. The scheme funds three levels of study. The recorded level is bachelor's, because the call page states three years of support for full-time bachelor's studies or for the first three years of a full-time joint bachelor's and master's degree programme, and two years of support for full-time master's studies. The master's coverage is recorded in programme_detail_official.degree_levels and in the description, not presented as this record's level; doctoral study is expressly excluded. STATUS. Registration for the 2026/2027 academic year is closed and the evaluation process is under way, so status is closed and no next-cycle dates are asserted. AMOUNTS. The only published amounts are EUR 500 per month, EUR 5,000 per academic year and a EUR 15,000 upper total; no other figure was computed. FAUNDING INVARIANTS. tuition_coverage is false because the scholarship is a living allowance and the scholarship page states that any tuition-fee waiver for foreign-language programmes is granted solely at the discretion of the higher education institution under Section 96(15) of Act No. 300/2025 Coll.; fully_funded is therefore false and living_cost_coverage is true. UNVERIFIED OR NOT READ. The official SK RIS3 2021+ programme list PDF and the country-category PDF linked from the call page returned 403 to direct fetching from this machine, so the lists are taken instead from the methodological document itself, which reproduces the five regional subgroups in Annex 13 and names the eligible higher education institutions. Language of instruction per programme, the individual admission requirements and deadlines of each higher education institution, and the fee amounts for foreign-language programmes were not read from an official source and are not stated here.

programme_detail_official.application_cycle: Academic year 2026/2027 round, closed on 8 September 2026. The scheme began under the predecessor Recovery and Resilience Plan scholarship call on 24 June 2025 and continued as the national project under the Slovakia Programme; the 2026/2027 methodological document was issued on 11 June 2026 in version 1.0.
programme_detail_official.deadline_central_display: 8 September 2026, 23:59 CEST (extended). The official application-procedure guide states the original deadline of 31 July 2026, 16:00 CEST.
programme_detail_official.deadline_note: The call page states that the application deadline was extended until 8 September 2026, 23:59 CEST, and the official application-procedure guide states the deadline of 31 July 2026, 16:00 CEST with the note that applications submitted after it cannot be accepted. CEST is the daylight-saving time in force on that date in Slovakia, recorded as Europe/Bratislava. deadline_institutional is null because the scholarship scheme itself sets no institutional deadline; each higher education institution sets its own admission deadlines in a separate admission procedure, and an applicant must apply to the institution directly and separately from this scholarship, so no institutional date is claimed. Evaluation takes place only after the applicants have been officially enrolled.
programme_detail_official.status_note: Registration for the academic year 2026/2027 is officially closed and the evaluation process is under way; the ministry states that selected recipients will be informed by the email address given at registration, through announcements published on the scholarship website, and through the status of the application in the applicant's personal account. Applicants must have enrolled by around September 2026 for the payments to begin. No opening date for a 2027/2028 round was published at the time of verification, so no next-cycle date is asserted; the predecessor call opened on 24 June 2025, which is the only published precedent.
programme_detail_official.funding_duration: Ten monthly payments in each academic year, from September to June. At the first level of study the scholarship is limited to the first three years of bachelor's study, or of a programme combining the first and second levels, that is academic years 2026/2027 to 2028/2029; for a standard four-year bachelor's programme only the first three years are funded. At the second level the scholarship is limited to two years of master's study, that is academic years 2026/2027 to 2027/2028.
programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: The scholarship is a living allowance and does not pay tuition fees. The call page states that scholarship recipients enrolled on a full-time programme taught in a foreign language at a public higher education institution may have their tuition fees waived in accordance with Section 96(15) of Act No. 300/2025 Coll. on Higher Education, but the waiver is granted exclusively at the decision of the higher education institution, so it cannot be counted as coverage of this award. Because tuition is not covered by the award itself, fully_funded is false and tuition_coverage is false.
programme_detail_official.funding_label: EUR 500 per month, ten months per academic year, EUR 5,000 per academic year and up to EUR 15,000 in total. A living allowance only: no tuition is paid by the award, any fee waiver for a foreign-language programme is at the discretion of the higher education institution, and travel, insurance, visa, accommodation and living costs above the allowance remain with the student. No bond or service obligation is published, but the award is tied to a specific full-time study programme at a specific higher education institution and cannot be transferred between institutions.

programme_detail_official.citizenship_residency: The applicant must be a national of a country other than Slovakia. Dual nationality that includes Slovak is allowed, and Slovaks living abroad with Slovak citizenship qualify by submitting the certificate issued under Section 7 of Act No. 474/2005 Coll. on Slovaks Living Abroad. The applicant must have had no permanent residence in Slovakia between 1 January 2021 and the application deadline. Studies completed outside Slovakia are not a bar to applying. At the bachelor's level the applicant must additionally not have studied at a secondary school or a higher education institution in Slovakia, with academic mobility the only exception.
programme_detail_official.international_eligibility: The scheme is open worldwide to nationals of any United Nations member state other than Slovakia, which the ministry describes as all international students worldwide including Slovaks living abroad. Registration with the United Nations is the criterion the methodology uses for the country lists: Annex 13 assigns every UN member state except Slovakia to one of five regional subgroups used only to structure the ranking. Applicants select their country of citizenship in the information system, which assigns them to the subgroup automatically, and territories that are not listed in any subgroup, such as unrecognised states, are assigned individually by the technical support desk on request.
programme_detail_official.study_mode: Full-time, in-person study only. The methodology states that the scholarship is tied to full-time study at a specific higher education institution, and that the entitlement ceases if the student changes from full-time to part-time or external study; no payment is made for a period of part-time enrolment.
programme_detail_official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The study programme must be one of the selected programmes falling under the Smart Specialisation Strategy of the Slovak Republic, SK RIS3 2021+ and its five identified domains: Innovative industry for the 21st century, Mobility for the 21st century, Intelligent transformation of Slovakia, Healthy society, and Food competitiveness and food self-sufficiency. The programme may be taught in Slovak or in a foreign language. Doctoral study is excluded, and private higher education institutions are excluded.
programme_detail_official.application_method: Separate competitive application by the student, submitted exclusively electronically online through the information system at https://scholarships.portalvs.sk/registration. It is not possible to request the scholarship by email. The award is not automatic on admission: a separate application for study must be submitted directly to the higher education institution of the applicant's choice, and the scholarship website may not be used for study applications.

programme_detail_official.selection_weighting: There is no academic or non-academic weighting. Regional redistribution is applied only when the number of eligible applications exceeds the number of scholarships allocated for that level and funding source; each funding source, the state budget and the national project, is ranked separately. Unused scholarships of a subgroup, where a subgroup has fewer eligible applicants than its primary allocation, move to the secondary selection.

programme_detail_official.description: A national scholarship scheme of the Ministry of Education, Research, Development and Youth of the Slovak Republic, funded from a national project co-financed by the European Union under the Slovakia Programme together with the state budget, and awarded to talented students from all over the world including Slovaks living abroad who study at selected public and state higher education institutions in Slovakia. In the 2026/2027 round the ministry allocated 170 scholarships at the first level of study, 110 financed from the national project for institutions outside the Bratislava region and 60 financed from the state budget for institutions in the Bratislava region, out of 1,431 talent scholarships in total and 1,040 at the first level. The scholarship is a living allowance of EUR 500 per month paid for the ten months from September to June in each of the first three academic years of full-time bachelor's or combined bachelor's and master's study, up to EUR 15,000 in total; doctoral study is excluded. Selection is made exclusively on the percentile score of the SAT, which requires a total of at least 1100 points, or of the two SCIO tests in Mathematics and General Academic Prerequisites, which require an average percentile of at least 63, and the supported programme must appear on the SK RIS3 2021+ list. Nineteen public and state higher education institutions are eligible, four of them in the Bratislava region and fifteen in other regions. Registration for the 2026/2027 round closed on 8 September 2026 and evaluation is under way.
programme_detail_official.coverage: A monthly living allowance of EUR 500 for ten months in each of the first three academic years of full-time bachelor's or combined bachelor's and master's study, up to EUR 5,000 per academic year and EUR 15,000 in total. Tuition fees are not paid by the award and any waiver of the fee for a foreign-language programme is at the sole discretion of the higher education institution; travel, health insurance, residence permit and visa costs, accommodation and living costs above the allowance all remain with the student. No installation allowance, travel allowance, research allowance, book or equipment allowance, family allowance or accommodation support is published.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm the round is open before relying on any date: registration for 2026/2027 is closed, so every date below applies to the 2027/2028 round only once the ministry announces it.

Book the SAT or the two SCIO tests early and make sure the certificate exists in hand before the deadline, because the certificate must be uploaded by the deadline and the result cannot be added afterwards.

Check that your SAT total is at least 1100 or your average SCIO percentile across Mathematics and General Academic Prerequisites is at least 63; below either threshold the application is not considered.
Confirm your SAT was taken on or after 1 January 2021 and before the application deadline; older scores are not accepted.
Get your passport or national identity card notarised before you start the online form; a plain scan or photograph of the original document is not accepted.
Write the curriculum vitae and the motivation letter in English in advance, and use the templates downloadable from the system, since both are described as essential documents.
Prepare the solemn declaration of permanent residence on the system template and sign it by hand, since only hand-signed declarations downloaded from the system are accepted.

If you are under 18 at the time of application, have your legal guardian complete and hand-sign the consent for the processing of your personal data, without which the application cannot be processed.
If you are a Slovak citizen living abroad, obtain the certificate under Section 7 of Act No. 474/2005 Coll. and have it notarised before applying.
Confirm you have had no permanent residence in Slovakia at any point between 1 January 2021 and the deadline, because there is no discretion for this condition.

If you studied at a Slovak secondary school or higher education institution, stop here: the award is closed to you except for academic mobility and for Slovaks living abroad with the Section 7 certificate.

Start a separate application for admission to the higher education institution in parallel, and start it early, because enrolling by around September is required for the scholarship to be paid at all.

Choose the institution and study programme from the published SK RIS3 2021+ list and from the nineteen eligible higher education institutions, and contact that institution's admissions office directly to confirm the language of instruction and its own admission requirements and deadlines.

Budget for everything the allowance does not cover, above all tuition fees if you are admitted to a foreign-language programme and the institution does not waive them, plus living costs, accommodation, health insurance, visa and residence permit costs and travel.
Submit the application fully before the deadline; an application left in the status in progress, even after the deadline, is never assessed.
common_rejection_risks: Leaving the application in the status in progress, which the ministry states is not accepted and is not assessed even after the deadline.

Submitting the test certificate after the deadline, or submitting a different test, since the scheme accepts only the SAT and the two SCIO tests and refuses AP, EST, CLT, ACT, GED, PSAT, NMSQT, PSAT 10, PSAT 8/9 and the secondary school leaving examination as substitutes.
Sitting only one of the two SCIO tests. The scheme requires both Mathematics (MAT) and General Academic Prerequisites (VŠP), and the average of the two percentiles must reach 63.
An SAT below 1100 or an average SCIO percentile below 63, which the ministry states excludes the applicant from consideration.
An SAT taken before 1 January 2021, which is outside the accepted period.
Uploading a plain scan or photograph of the passport instead of a notarised copy, which the ministry states is not sufficient.
A solemn declaration that is not hand-signed, or not downloaded from the system, since only hand-signed declarations downloaded from the system are accepted.
Choosing a study programme that is not on the SK RIS3 2021+ list, because the scholarship is granted only if the applicant enrols on a listed programme.
Applying to a private higher education institution, which the methodology excludes from the support.
Holding permanent residence in Slovakia at any point between 1 January 2021 and the deadline.
Having studied at a Slovak secondary school or, at the bachelor's level, at a Slovak higher education institution, with academic mobility the only exception.
Enrolling part-time or external, which ends the entitlement and stops payment for that period.
Failing to enrol by the autumn of the intake year, since the scholarship is paid only to an officially enrolled student and the evaluation takes place after enrolment.
Transferring to another higher education institution after the award, which the ministry states is not possible.
Repeating a year or restarting the selected programme, which the methodology states cannot be paid.
Any falsified or altered document, which results in withdrawal from the scholarship and an obligation to repay the amounts already awarded.
Assuming the scholarship guarantees admission, when the ministry states that receiving it does not mean acceptance or enrolment at a higher education institution.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees. The award pays a living allowance only. Where the applicant enrols on a programme taught in a foreign language, a waiver may be granted at the sole discretion of the higher education institution under Section 96(15) of Act No. 300/2025 Coll., so plan as if tuition is payable and confirm the fee and the waiver decision in writing with the chosen institution before committing.

Living costs above EUR 500 per month. The ministry describes the scholarship as a motivational tool intended, for example but not exclusively, to cover living costs, so the full cost of living in the study city must be met from other funds.
Accommodation and dormitory rent, which the award does not cover and which the student must arrange directly with the institution or on the private market.

Public health insurance for applicants not insured in another EU, EEA or Swiss state. Coverage is conditional under Act No. 580/2004 Coll. on the programme being approved by the Government of the Slovak Republic, so verify the position with the chosen institution rather than assuming cover.

Visa and residence costs for non-EU nationals: the ministry recommends a 120-day national D visa applied for at the Embassy of the Slovak Republic abroad or through an accredited external service provider, followed by temporary residence for the purpose of study within those 120 days.
Travel to and from Slovakia in both directions, which the award does not cover.
Study materials, equipment and any laboratory, fieldwork or practice costs, none of which is published as covered.

Admission-related costs at the higher education institution, including recognition of the foreign secondary-school certificate and any language or preparatory course, which are governed by the institution's own admission procedure and not by this scheme.
Lost earnings or opportunity cost during the three years of funded study, which no allowance of this size addresses.
document_audit: This list is derived guidance for assembling the official checklist, not an official requirement in itself; the official list is the eight items published on the call page.
Passport for most nationalities, or national identity card for citizens of the European Union, the European Economic Area and Switzerland, and it must be a notarised copy, not a scan or photograph.
Solemn declaration of permanent residence, downloaded from the system template and hand-signed, stating no permanent residence in Slovakia between 1 January 2021 and the application deadline.

SAT certificate showing the date, the total score and the partial scores in Evidence-Based Reading and Writing and in Mathematics, or the two official SCIO certificates showing the date and percentile for Mathematics (MAT) and for General Academic Prerequisites (VŠP).
Curriculum vitae in English, structured and on the template from the system, which the ministry states is an essential document for the evaluation of the application.

Motivation letter in English on the template from the system, explaining the motivation for studying in Slovakia and describing the applicant's talent characteristics, which the ministry also states is essential.
Consent of the legal guardian for the processing of the minor applicant's personal data, for applicants under 18, completed and hand-signed by the legal guardian.
Certificate under Section 7 of Act No. 474/2005 Coll. on Slovaks Living Abroad, certified, for Slovak applicants living abroad.
Acceptance letter from the higher education institution, if one is already available, since the call page lists it as an optional attachment.

Keep proof of submission, since the ministry states that once an application is submitted it can no longer be edited and attachments cannot be added or removed, and request any correction through technical support.

alerts.message: Registration for the academic year 2026/2027 closed on 8 September 2026 at 23:59 CEST and the evaluation is under way. Nothing can be submitted for this round; monitor https://scholarships.portalvs.sk/ for the next call, and note that no opening date for the next round had been published as at 3 October 2026.

The ministry states that the result of the chosen standardised test is the only criterion for the selection of successful applicants. A strong academic record, a strong motivation letter or a strong CV cannot compensate for a test score below the threshold of an SAT total of 1100 or an average SCIO percentile of 63.

Applying to this scholarship does not apply you to the institution, and the scholarship may not be used for study applications. Apply directly to the higher education institution of your choice, and enrol by around September, because the scholarship is paid only after enrolment and the evaluation takes place after enrolment.

alerts.trigger: Programme must be on the SK RIS3 list
alerts.message: The scholarship is granted only if you enrol on a programme from the SK RIS3 2021+ list. You may apply with a preferred programme that is not on the list, but the scholarship will then not be granted, so check the published list before you choose.

This award is a living allowance. Any waiver of the tuition fee for a foreign-language programme is at the exclusive discretion of the higher education institution under Section 96(15) of Act No. 300/2025 Coll. and is not guaranteed by this scholarship, so treat tuition as payable until the institution confirms otherwise.

The 60 state-budget scholarships are reserved for students at institutions in the Bratislava region and the 110 national-project scholarships for institutions outside it. Each pool is ranked separately, so a strong applicant may be funded in one pool and not the other; your choice of institution can therefore change the outcome.

The scholarship is tied to a specific full-time programme at a specific higher education institution, and a change of institution is not possible after the award. Choose your institution before applying, because you cannot shop between institutions after receiving the scholarship.

If you were ever a pupil or graduate of a Slovak secondary school, or a student of a Slovak higher education institution at the bachelor's level, you are not eligible. The only exception is academic mobility, and the only further exception is for Slovaks living abroad submitting the Section 7 certificate.

alerts.trigger: Documents cannot be edited after submission
alerts.message: Once the application is submitted it can no longer be edited and attachments cannot be added or removed. Check every field and every attachment before submitting, and contact technical support during the application period if you spot an error.

submission_workflow: Monitor https://scholarships.portalvs.sk/ for the announcement that registration is open for the next academic year, since no opening date was published for the round after 2026/2027 at the time of verification.
Sit the SAT or the two SCIO tests early, and confirm the score meets the threshold of an SAT total of 1100 or an average SCIO percentile of 63 before the round opens.
Create a user account at https://scholarships.portalvs.sk/registration when the round opens.

Select the level of study, then the preferred higher education institution, faculty and study programme, checking first that the programme appears on the SK RIS3 2021+ list and that the institution is one of the nineteen eligible public or state higher education institutions.

Enter the standardised test result: for the SAT, the date, the total score and the partial scores in Evidence-Based Reading and Writing and in Mathematics; for the SCIO tests, the date and percentile for each of the Mathematics (MAT) and General Academic Prerequisites (VŠP) tests, which the system averages automatically.

Upload the notarised identity document, the hand-signed solemn declaration of permanent residence, and where applicable the Section 7 certificate for Slovaks living abroad and the guardian's consent for minors.
Upload the structured curriculum vitae in English and the motivation letter in English, both on the system templates.
Review the application summary, then press submit. The application is valid only once it has been submitted and will remain unassessed if it stays in progress.

Watch for the automatic confirmation email, and note that the application cannot be edited after submission, so any correction must be requested through technical support during the application period.

After the deadline, the ministry verifies eligibility and the authenticity of documents and compiles the final ranking, which is published on https://scholarships.portalvs.sk/ and communicated by email and through the status of the application account.

Enrol in the first year of the supported full-time programme by around September, because the ministry or the higher education institution verifies and evaluates applications only after enrolment and the institution then issues the Decision on the Award of the Scholarship.

Sign the scholarship contract, then receive the payments from the higher education institution, normally in arrears, with all eligible September months paid retroactively in the first instalment if there has been a delay.

programme_detail_verification.cycle_verified: Academic year 2026/2027 round of the Scholarships for talented students from all over the world, closed 8 September 2026, verified 2026-10-03
official_fields_confirmed: award identity and official full name, from the call page heading "Scholarships for talented students from all over the world (academic year 2026/2027)
administering authority: Ministry of Education, Research, Development and Youth of the Slovak Republic

funding instrument and sources: national project co-financed by the European Union under the Slovakia Programme together with the state budget, with separate pools for institutions inside and outside the Bratislava region

allocation at the first level: 170 scholarships, 110 financed from the national project for institutions outside the Bratislava region and 60 from the state budget for institutions in the Bratislava region, from the allocation table in the methodological document
allocation at the second level: 55 scholarships, 35 and 20 respectively, and the scheme-wide totals of 1431 talent scholarships, 1040 at the first level and 391 at the second
amount: EUR 500 per month, paid for ten months in each academic year, EUR 5,000 per academic year, up to EUR 15,000 in total

duration at the first level: first three academic years of bachelor's or combined bachelor's and master's study, academic years 2026/2027 to 2028/2029, with only three years funded for a four-year bachelor's programme
payment mechanics: paid in the full monthly amount for any month of enrolment, in arrears, retroactively in the first instalment where needed, with no payment for July or August
geographic grouping: five regional subgroups B1 Europe, B2 United States, Canada, Australia and Oceania, B3 Central and South America, B4 Africa and B5 Asia, with the full country lists in Annex 13

regional redistribution rule: ten per cent of the allocated scholarships per funding source awarded per subgroup, that is fifty per cent in total, with the remaining fifty per cent by percentile score without regional redressement
selection criterion: the standardised test result is the only criterion, converted to a common percentile scale of 0 to 100

test requirement: SAT total of at least 1100 points, or an average percentile of at least 63 across the SCIO Mathematics (MAT) and General Academic Prerequisites (VŠP) tests, with no substitution or waiver
test validity: SAT results accepted from 1 January 2021 until the application deadline; SCIO results must be evidenced by an official SCIO certificate
deadline: 8 September 2026 at 23:59 CEST, extended from 31 July 2026 at 16:00 CEST
status: registration for 2026/2027 closed, evaluation under way
supported fields of study: only programmes on the SK RIS3 2021+ list, across the five smart specialisation domains, with doctoral study excluded
eligible institutions: nineteen public and state higher education institutions, four in the Bratislava region and fifteen in other regions, with private institutions excluded

eligible countries: nationals of any United Nations member state other than Slovakia, with Slováks living abroad qualifying through the Section 7 certificate and dual nationality including Slovak permitted

eligibility conditions: notarised identity document, no permanent residence in Slovakia since 1 January 2021, no prior secondary or higher education study in Slovakia except academic mobility, full-time in-person study, no upper age limit, guardian consent for minors
required documents: the eight items published on the call page

renewal and loss conditions: the entitlement ceases on termination of study, transfer to another institution, change to part-time study, or interruption of study exceeding 180 days in individual or total duration
concurrent funding: the scholarship may be held with other scholarships and with mobility funding, provided there is no duplicate support for the same purpose

health insurance: public insurance available under Act No. 580/2004 Coll. for holders of a scholarship under a programme approved by the Government of the Slovak Republic who are not insured in another EU, EEA or Swiss state
tuition: not covered; a waiver for foreign-language programmes is at the sole discretion of the higher education institution under Section 96(15) of Act No. 300/2025 Coll.
application method: exclusively online through the official information system, not by email, and separate from the study application at the institution
logo bytes served by the awarding body's own domain
degree level: the call page funds three years of full-time bachelor's or combined bachelor's and master's study, so bachelor's is the level recorded

research_notes.logo: The awarding body is the Ministry of Education, Research, Development and Youth of the Slovak Republic, so the logo was taken from the ministry's own domain rather than from the scholarship portal. The ministry's English pages render their own mark as /assets/default/img/logo-minedu-en.svg in the header, and that URL was probed live and returned HTTP 200 with Content-Type image/svg+xml and 18867 bytes, with an SVG body that begins with an XML prologue and a DOCTYPE, satisfying the rule that a host whose logo URL returns HTML rather than image bytes is excluded. Rule 6 was checked rather than assumed: a colour audit of the eight path elements found six filled rgb(0,76,152) ministry blue, two rgb(227,6,19) red and one rgb(218,218,218) light grey, with a single white detail, so this is a dark mark safe on a light card, not a white-on-transparent wordmark; the white counterpart logo-minedu-en-white.svg that the ministry also publishes was deliberately not used. research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: The scholarship call page states three years of support for the applicant's full-time bachelor's degree studies or for the first three years of a full-time joint bachelor's and master's degree study programme, alongside two years of support for full-time master's studies, and the ministry's own page for the previous round describes the scheme as intended for applicants planning study in bachelor's, combined bachelor's and master's, or master's programmes. The methodological document allocates 170 scholarships to subgroup B1, the foreign talented students at the first level of study, which is the bachelor's or combined level, and 55 to subgroup B2 at the second level, and it restricts first-level support to the first three years of bachelor's or combined study, funding only three years even where the standard length of the bachelor's programme is four years. Doctoral study is expressly excluded. Bachelor's is therefore the level recorded in new_scholarship.degree_levels, with the master's and combined coverage recorded in programme_detail_official.degree_levels and in the description rather than presented as this record's level.
